newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures rebound from Friday slide.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures rebound from Friday slide.

text.p: Most U.S. stock index futures rebounded from Friday's slide and posted strong early gains in very brisk trading.
September Standard and Poor's 500 futures moved higher in fast market trade led by broad-based, but nervous, early buying.
Players were encouraged by September's performance on Globex after-hours electronic trade, as the market managed to creep above 900.00 support in active overnight trade.
"I'm looking for some sort of recovery," an S&P 500 futures floor analyst said.
"I'm not going to give up yet," the analyst said.
On Friday, September S&Ps crumbled to the lowest price in 6-1/2-weeks and the Dow Jones Industrial average fell 247 points in its largest one-day point drop since the October 1987 crash.

Traders and analysts had anxiously watched Sunday Globex trade for clues to the market's direction for Monday, and many noted the failure of September to violently follow through on the downside from Friday's losses. They said brisk Globex volume and mostly rangebound activity was a good sign for Monday's early action.
Floor traders noted initial resistance Monday at 904.75, but September soon pierced that level to reach a peak of 908.00 for the day.
Traders said three firms were aggressive buyers on the open, with one of those then turning a seller and briefly stalling the morning's gains.
Optima Technical Research pegged a pivot point in September at 909.10 and the 50-day average at 921.85.
One firm pegged September S&P 500 fair value at 3.35 points premium to cash, buy programs at 4.70 points premium to cash or wider and sells at 1.60 points premium or narrower.
The Chicago Mercantile Exchange estimated Friday's overall S&P 500 volume at 71,082 contracts, up slightly from Thursday's 60,582.

At 0917 CDT/1417 GMT, Sept S&P 500s rose 7.70 to 906.25, Midcap 400s rose 0.10 to 309.00, Russell 2000 was flat at 410.50, Value Lines rose 4.50 pts to 826.50, NYSE Composite rose 2.80 to 470.40, NASDAQ rose 6.50 to 1079.00, and Nikkei rose 165.0 to 19,195.00.
